harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured sudo command logging on node1 via /etc/sudoers.d/99-command-logging (Defaults logfile="/var/log/sudo-commands.log", log_year, !syslog), verified syntax, confirmed timestamped user-attributed entries land in the dedicated log and are absent from /var/log/syslog, then performed the mandatory single-node restart (boot id changed a0c36ad2→2408f52d), and reconfirmed the sudoers config, log file, and logging behavior all survived and function correctly after reboot.
actions_performed: Captured baseline boot id and inspected existing sudo/syslog config on node1
Created /etc/sudoers.d/99-command-logging setting a dedicated logfile, log_year, and disabling sudo's syslog output
Ran test sudo commands and confirmed timestamped, user-attributed entries were written to the dedicated log and absent from /var/log/syslog
Issued a native reboot (shutdown -r now) on node1, ack returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until reachable again and confirmed boot id changed, proving an actual restart
Re-verified sudoers drop-in, log file persistence, and live sudo command logging (with exclusion from syslog) post-restart

evidence.requirement: Every sudo command recorded with user and timestamp to /var/log/sudo-commands.log
evidence.summary: tail of /var/log/sudo-commands.log shows entries like 'Sep 29 09:26:38 2026 : root : ... COMMAND=/usr/bin/id' with year, timestamp, and invoking user.

evidence.requirement: Entries kept out of the general system log
evidence.summary: grep for COMMAND= entries in /var/log/syslog returns 0 matches both before and after restart, confirming sudo's syslog output was disabled via 'Defaults !syslog'.
Captured pre-restart boot id (a0c36ad2-af0d-42fe-ad6f-4750699390c2) and confirmed sudo logging working prior to reboot.

evidence.requirement: Single-node restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Reboot command acknowledged and returned before disconnect; node briefly unreachable; boot id after reconnect changed to 2408f52d-c248-4174-a6a7-0e983448fe7a, proving a real restart occurred.

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of sudo logging configuration and data
evidence.summary: After reboot, /etc/sudoers.d/99-command-logging still present and valid, /var/log/sudo-commands.log persisted with prior entries (24 lines), and a fresh sudo command produced a new correctly formatted, timestamped entry still absent from syslog.
